pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

As per title

Fixes: https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/923
Fixes: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/26899

This PR adds NEFTune: a new technique for enhancing Supervised fine-tuning results results proposed in: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05914 

![Screenshot 2023-10-13 at 17 36 38](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/assets/49240599/81995c1d-16c3-4cfc-9fbc-0701a9a87531)


I propose a very simple API which is as simple as passing a valid `neftune_noise_alpha` argument when initializing the `TrainingArguments`. To avoid any surprising behaviour, we should revert to the original forward method at the end of the training. This is handled inside the inner training loop that attaches the correct forward hook before the beginning of training, and makes sure to remove it right after training the model.

issue_context.title: NEFTune Support pls
issue_context.body:
### Feature request

The TRL library introduced support for NEFTune in this [pr](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/871) 

### Motivation

Improves Supervised Fine-tuning performance

See paper : https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05914

### Your contribution

I can try to port code over from TRL.
comments: Hey @nivibilla, we integrate well with TRL, which leverages a hefty number of components from the `transformers` library. What is your issue with the current TRL implementation/what would you like to enable by moving the support from TRL directly to `transformers` ?
a lot of my scripts and pipelines for finetuning use native transformers. ideally I don't want to have to update all of them to use trl if possible.

@younesbelkada could you share a bit about how one could go about leveraging NEFTune with `transformers` models?

I think it's important that the two frameworks complete each other rather than compete for the same features with differing implementations, so let's take a look at leveraging TRL simply for `transformers` models rather than importing the implementation within `transformers`.

currently in TRL we monkey-patch the forward pass of the emebdding layer with a new one, but with https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/889 we'll have a cleaner implementation that leverage forward post hooks which is cleaner. I will open a PR to add that feature in Trainer and leverage that feature in TRL

review_comments: A check should be made that it's correctly disabled after training has finished

the line 
```python
self.assertTrue(len(trainer.model.get_input_embeddings()._forward_hooks) == 0)
```
Should check if the forward hook as been correctly removed so I think all should be good here
Note also that line is called right after training, so it should check that neftune is correctly disabled after training.
Added slightly more elaborated test in [ca8f8c4](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/27141/commits/ca8f8c43f662f55e367bb035fa2a51abf78fc794)
